title: Newcastle sign Mohamed Diamé from Hull City on a three-year contract
trail: Newcastle have announced the signing of Mohamed Diamé from Hull City with the 29-year-old Senegal international agreeing a three-year deal
body: Newcastle United have announced the signing of Mohamed Diamé from Hull City. The Senegal international has agreed a three-year deal and becomes the eighth player to join Rafael Benítez’s first-team squad this summer. Diamé, 29, began his career with the French side Lens before moving to Spain, where he played for Linares and Rayo Vallecano. He joined Wigan Athletic in August 2009 and has spent the past seven years in England, where he also played for West Ham United. “It is a great feeling to be a Newcastle player,” he said. “Everybody close to me knows how desperate I am to play in the Premier League again, but when Newcastle comes in for you it makes you think. “I am looking to the future. Newcastle is a big name, a massive club and will be back in the Premier League, for sure.” Benítez, the Newcastle manager, said: “Mohamed is a strong, attack-minded player with a lot of fight and determination to his game. He is also someone who will provide the team with goals and assists from midfield. “He has good experience of the Championship and the fight needed to win promotion, which will be important for us.” On a busy day for Benítez, Newcastle unveiled the signing of Ciaran Clark from their Championship rivals Aston Villa. The versatile 26-year-old, who can play at centre-back, left-back or in a holding midfield role, has signed a five-year deal after Newcastle activated the £5.1m break clause in his contract. “Ciaran is a very versatile player, as a left-footed centre-back he can also play left-back and also as a defensive midfielder,” Benítez said. “He has a lot of experience of English football and will add good balance and competition to our squad. I am sure he will progress with us here at Newcastle, we are very happy for him to join us.” Clark came through the ranks at Villa before making his debut for the club in August 2009, while still a teenager. He soon became a regular in the side and over the following six seasons went on to make more than 150 appearances, scoring 10 goals. Clark has won 19 caps for Ireland and represented his country this summer at the European Championship in France, scoring an unfortunate own goal in their 1-1 draw with Sweden.
